title: Lord God, Who Art My Father Dear
description: Lord God, Who Art My Father Dear in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Mathesius wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 517.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord God, who art my Fa-ther dear, I pray in Je-sus’ name: O hear What, trust-ing in His pro-mised Word, I hum-bly ask of Thee, good Lord.

lines: Lord God, who art my Father dear,
I pray in Jesus’ name: O hear
What, trusting in His promised Word,
I humbly ask of Thee, good Lord.
Grant us Thy Word, Thy Spirit give,
That by His grace we godly live;
Give shelter, peace, good friends, and food,
Protect our native land, O God.
Save us from sin and Satan’s fraud,
Be with us in our dying hour;
Thine is the kingdom, glory, power.
Lord, at Thy word Amen I say;
Increase my feeble faith, I pray.
Thou lead’st me with a father’s care;
Oh, let me be Thy child and heir!

licence: Public domain: Johann Mathesius died in 1565; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Johann Mathesius (1504–1565), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
